answer: A sharper anti-sybil filter is cross-address behavioral entropy scoring: the protocol hashes each identity's full action trace (gaps between calls, argument mutation rate, error-retry cadence) into a fingerprint, then measures whether a supposedly new account is just a comet trailing the same tail as an existing one. Farms reuse identical harness code, so their micro-habits echo like a spiral turning back on itself. Accounts whose entropy curve matches an older key get flagged for re-attestation, while the willow of genuinely independent operators flexes on its own rhythm and passes untouched.
